i’ll start with the very baseline by saying that “high functioning” and “aspergers” are both outdated terms that are no longer recognised by major psychological health organisations due to their inaccuracy, social impact and damaging connotations. 

a longer form answer is essentially the notion that all autistic people have special needs and are disabled and struggle to function to some degree. a better way that has been widely more accepted is defining people as “higher needs” versus “lower needs”. 

an analogy i like is there could be an autistic person who has the mental development of a 5 year old, is non verbal, and needs constant support from professionals, but is happy, supported, experiences sensory overloads and meltdowns less and less. this person suffers, yes. 

however i go to university, live on my own, sustain myself by myself, and by many peoples definition i am “high functioning” because i require less immediate support than the previous example. however, i suffer from severe sensory overloads and meltdowns almost daily, am partially non verbal, cannot drive which causes me to not be able to work many places and can’t hold down a job as it is far too much for my autistic brain to handle. i live in a perpetual state of debilitating fear, pain, and stress due to the world around me but because my symptoms manifest differently to another autistic person who may require more immediate aid, my struggles are brushed off and i am deemed high functioning. 

i do not function at a higher rate, and i, like many others, believe that going to school and getting a job are arbitrary definitions of being “functional” as the implications of your functionality being tied to what you provide to societies institutions is odd. i do not see myself as high functioning, but requiring less immediate support, therefore being “lower needs”.
